description: A team from Kuching in Malaysia here !!
summary: This is our team's project summary. To solve one of the challenge given, which is Abandoned but Not Forgotten ( NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon & Mars ), we made a 30-seconds long, animated video of a character that brings the audience exploring the discarded equipment and explain the equipment journey and usage. A bright coloured animation is to keep the audience engaged with the topic, so they could learn what else has the humanity left in space and what they have been working on. In this way, both art and historical events can be continued to be expressed to generation by generation. Furthermore, as we are hoping that our project could make the audience to keep questioning and exploring about historical events until an ongoing missions that are related to space, more likely, STEM. In addition, it is important for us to develop a creation that could ignite back all of these back to life, because in this way, all of the hard work and appreciation will be remembered when audience leave with a feeling of wanting to keep exploring that could be helpful in the future and for younger people
details: This project is made by hand-drawn animation. Instead of boring and static presentation slides, it is animated to keep the audience engaged with the video while it explains about the discarded equipment. Its benefits showed when the audience leave with a feeling of connection to this exploration about the equipment, complex NASA's data is translated to simpler to help young audience to understand, learnt new art styles and creativity. We hope teachers will use this tool in classrooms to get kids excited about space science. We used apps like Capcut, Ibispaintx, Flipaclip, Alight Motion and ElevenLabs for this animation. We made sure that this animation looks entertaining to watch by all age audience.
